newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt hunts for gunmen who shot 14 in two attacks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt hunts for gunmen who shot 14 in two attacks.

text.p: Egyptian security forces on Friday searched for gunmen who went on a deadly rampage in a southern Egypt hamlet, shooting passersby in the head and neck and killing 13 people, a doctor and police said.
Security sources said they suspected Moslem militants were responsible for the Thursday night massacre and the killing of a woman a few hours later.

"Everyone arrived dead except for one. They were shot in the head and neck except for the one who arrived still gasping, because the bullet tore his liver," said a doctor at a hospital near Ezbet Dawoud, where the first attack occurred.
"We put him in intensive care for operating and he died on the table," the doctor, who declined to be named, told Reuters by telephone from the Nag Hammadi hospital.
A 40-year-old woman died and seven people were wounded in the second attack, the Interior Ministry said.
Security sources said in the second attack gunmen fired on a train which had stopped in Nag Hammadi on its way from Aswan to Cairo. They put the number of wounded at 15.
Police manned roadblocks and combed sugar cane fields in the southern Qena province to hunt down the gunmen.
"It was a total surprise. We still don't know why it happened," a police officer told Reuters by telephone from Nag Hammadi, about 450 km (280 miles) south of Cairo.

Security sources said the gunmen, armed with automatic rifles, first opened fire at a tailor's shop, killing its owner and another man. They continued walking along the main road, shooting at passersby, the sources said.
Their rampage lasted about 30 minutes before they fled into sugar cane fields.
It was one of the bloodiest attacks since militants launched their campaign in 1992 to overthrow the government and turn Egypt into a strict Islamic state.
The people in Ezbet Dawoud are mainly Coptic Christians. A list of victims' names released by the Interior Ministry indicated that eight were Christians.
The victims included farmers, labourers and grocers ranging in age from 20 years to the mid-60s, according to the statement.
Egyptian police are still looking for five men they suspect of massacring 10 Coptic Christians in an attack on a church in Minya province last month.

Security sources said they believed the gunmen were from the al-Gama'a al-Islamiyah (Islamic Group) which has attacked trains in southern Egypt in the past because they sometimes carry tourists -- once targets in the group's anti-government drive.
The group has also targeted ministers, policemen and Christians in its armed campaign.
More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence in Egypt since militants took up arms.
